There are several inaccuracies in this statement.

First, the B permit is a temporary residence permit issued for the purpose of gainful employment. Its validity period can vary significantly depending on the specific circumstances and the type of employment contract. It is **not universally limited to one year**. The permit is often issued for the duration of a specific job contract, but if the employment is expected to be longer-term, it can be issued for a longer period. There is no universal rule that it must be only one year.

Second, an open-ended (unlimited) employment contract is one possible way to obtain a B permit, but it is **not an absolute requirement**. The permit can also be issued for fixed-term contracts. The key requirements generally include having a confirmed job offer, meeting specific qualifications (depending on the job), and fulfilling other legal requirements such as accommodation and health insurance. The nature of the employment contract (fixed-term vs. open-ended) is a factor, but not a strict barrier.

For precise and up-to-date information, always consult the official website of the Swiss State Secretariat for Migration (SEM) or contact your local cantonal migration authority, as regulations can evolve and vary based on individual cases, job categories, and nationality.
